summary: Address code smell: shotgun surgery data locals in opencode terminals

delivery.outcome: Rename the generic local variable 'data' to stage-accurate names in each of the nine functions of src/koruapi/opencode_terminals.py that mutate it: registry_entries (load_registry, parsed registry file content), request_body (_api_request, encoded outbound request bytes), health (instance_health, health probe payload), session_payload (list_sessions), catalog_payload (list_providers, matching its provider-catalog docstring), config_payload (get_instance_config), creation_payload (create_session), message_payload (session_messages), request_payload (pending_requests, per-kind pending response). The code2llm shotgun-surgery detector groups mutations by (file, variable) and fires at >= 5 scopes; the 'data' group drops from 9 scopes to 0. Each new name is a distinct local used in exactly one function, so no (file, variable) group grows. Pure rename of function-internal locals; the urllib Request data= keyword and the API envelope key "data" keep their names; no behavior change. The four separate pre-existing shotgun findings in the file (entry, url, out, text) are untouched by design.
nonGoals: No behavior, API-envelope-key, endpoint or interface change
No restructuring into a response-envelope wrapper class (each local already names one endpoint's decoded response; the shared generic name was the defect, not a missing abstraction)
No rename of the urllib request data= parameter, the JSON envelope key "data", or locals in other files
No fix for the separate pre-existing shotgun findings in this file (entry, url, out, text) - minimal scope for this ticket's reported smell only

architecture.decision: Stage-accurate local renames only, inside one module. Every function that holds a decoded endpoint response names it after the stage it serves (registry file, outbound body, health probe, per-endpoint payloads); the generic name 'data' disappears from the file's mutation set entirely. Verified with the installed code2llm ProjectAnalyzer + SmellDetector._detect_shotgun_surgery on the src/koruapi package: baseline reports 'Shotgun Surgery: data' at line 458 (9 mutating scopes, exactly matching the ticket) plus four other pre-existing findings; after the rename 'Shotgun Surgery: data' is gone, the file's mutation count is unchanged (310) and the four other findings are unchanged.
architecture.rollback: Revert the ticket commit; the locals are named data again and the smell report returns.

commands: python3 -c "<standalone code2llm ProjectAnalyzer.analyze_project(<repo>/src/koruapi) + SmellDetector._detect_shotgun_surgery, original vs renamed content of src/koruapi/opencode_terminals.py>"
validation.evidence: Deterministic ground truth with the installed code2llm detector on the package directory (single-file analysis yields empty function scopes and silently misses smells, so the package dir is required). Baseline content reports 'Shotgun Surgery: data' at line 458 - matching the ticket's file, line and dedupe key exactly - driven by 9 mutating scopes (_api_request, create_session, get_instance_config, instance_health, list_providers, list_sessions, load_registry, pending_requests, session_messages). Renamed content reports no 'Shotgun Surgery: data'; file mutation count unchanged at 310 (pure rename); no new (file, variable) group reaches the >= 5 threshold. The four separate pre-existing findings (entry, url, out, text) are unchanged by design.

Both suites covering src/koruapi/opencode_terminals.py pass unchanged (pure rename of function-internal locals; the suites exercise list_sessions, session_messages, pending_requests, get_instance_config, terminal helpers and the /proc scan through the public functions) and ruff reports zero errors on the touched file. Full-suite baseline comparison done against a clean base checkout so pre-existing environmental reds are not attributed to this change.
GOV-PASS 0 errors 0 warnings from the ticket worktree with the changed files declared.
